gloss: to settle down to, to commit seriously

definitions.gloss: to settle down, to commit seriously to a task
definitions.explanation: To approach something with serious, sustained effort; to buckle down and work diligently.

definitions.gloss: to settle in a place, to stay put
definitions.explanation: To establish oneself in a location for a considerable time.

examples.japanese: {腰|こし}を{据|す}えて{勉強|べんきょう}する{時間|じかん}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: I need time to buckle down and study seriously.

examples.japanese: この{問題|もんだい}には{腰|こし}を{据|す}えて{取|と}り{組|く}むべきだ。
examples.english: We should tackle this problem with serious commitment.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}に{腰|こし}を{据|す}えて{研究|けんきゅう}することにした。
examples.english: I decided to settle in Kyoto and conduct my research.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {腰|こし} (waist/hip) + を + {据|す}える (to set, place firmly). Literally 'to set one's hips down' - the image of sitting down firmly to work.

NUANCE: Implies sustained, serious effort rather than casual or superficial engagement. Suggests patience and dedication.

CONTRAST WITH OTHER {腰|こし} EXPRESSIONS:
- {腰|こし}を{据|す}える: to commit, settle down
- {腰|こし}が{重|おも}い: slow to act, reluctant to start
- {腰|こし}が{低|ひく}い: humble in manner
- {腰|こし}が{軽|かる}い: quick to act, easy-going

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- じっくり{取|と}り{組|く}む (to work on carefully)
- {本腰|ほんごし}を{入|い}れる (to put serious effort into)
- {腰|こし}を{落|お}ち{着|つ}ける (to settle down)
